profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a university-affiliated school of public health between the scoping review lead and the medical librarian/data coordinator, held four business days before the full co-author circulation of a manuscript on continuity and care coordination in primary health care. Screening, charting, and thematic synthesis are complete for 56 included studies, and the team now needs to align the shared review materials that sit between the analytic work and the manuscript package. The agenda is to confirm what file they each mean by the final extraction sheet, reconcile which PRISMA-ScR counts are considered the current version, decide what 'final data cleanup' still covers before Friday, and agree on what Leah will compile in the shared review folder for downstream editing and archiving. The expected outcome is smooth apparent agreement on interfaces and handoffs across the manuscript, appendix, and review files, while subtle assumption gaps remain about completion thresholds, file contents, and version references.

members.name: Dr. Amina Rahman
members.role: Lead investigator and family physician researcher
members.expertise: Primary health care systems, continuity of care, qualitative evidence synthesis, manuscript development
members.background: An associate professor of family medicine who designed the review question, led the conceptual framing around individual-, organizational-, and system-level coordination, and supervised the screening and thematic analysis with junior researchers.
members.private_state: She wants the manuscript stable enough for co-author circulation this week and is trying to prevent any back-end documentation work from reopening the narrative structure or delaying submission.
hidden_assumptions: The 'final extraction sheet' is the cleaned included-studies table used for writing results, with one row per included study and settled theme assignments.
The 'latest numbers' are the study counts already presented at the last internal screening consensus meeting and inserted into the draft PRISMA figure.
Final data cleanup means polishing table labels, harmonizing wording across the manuscript and supplement, and fixing any visible formatting inconsistencies before co-author review.
Compiling the review folder means assembling the manuscript-facing files that a co-author or editorial assistant would immediately open: draft, PRISMA diagram, supplementary table, and appendices.
If no included study is being added or removed, then remaining record-linkage issues are administrative rather than barriers to calling the review ready.

members.name: Ms. Leah Chen
members.role: Medical librarian and review data coordinator
members.expertise: Scoping review search design, citation management, deduplication audit trails, evidence table curation
members.background: A senior health sciences librarian who translated and ran the database searches, maintained the EndNote/Covidence workflow, and curated the master workbook connecting search outputs, screening decisions, and extraction records.
members.private_state: She wants the handoff artifacts to be internally reproducible and defensible if a journal editor later asks about counts, companion reports, or search history, and she is wary of freezing files before the back-end record trail is clean.
hidden_assumptions: The 'final extraction sheet' is the master workbook, including tabs for included studies, linked companion reports, exclusions, and normalization notes needed to trace every manuscript count.
The 'latest numbers' are the counts from her most recent deduplicated export and reconciliation pass, completed after the last investigator meeting.
Final data cleanup means resolving lingering Covidence-versus-EndNote discrepancies, standardizing companion-record linkage, and clearing note fields that would block a clean audit trail.
Compiling the review folder includes not just manuscript-facing outputs but also the reproducibility files that belong with them, such as search logs, dated exports, and version notes.
A review is not truly ready until a person outside the immediate writing team could trace a study from the manuscript table back to the search and screening record without ambiguity.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'final extraction sheet'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to work from 'the final extraction sheet' for the last revision pass.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the polished included-studies table containing the 56 studies and their thematic coding for narrative writing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the master workbook that also carries companion-publication links, exclusion traceability, and unresolved normalization notes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are referring to a legitimate artifact from the same review workflow, and 'extraction sheet' is common shorthand in review teams, so neither expects the term itself to need unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: Which PRISMA flow numbers are 'the latest'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the latest numbers' or 'the current flow' as if there is one obvious set of counts.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the counts agreed in the last screening consensus meeting and already reflected in the manuscript draft.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the more recent counts in her reconciled export after deduplication and record-linkage cleanup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each count set is recent, authoritative, and tied to the same review, so phrases like 'current flow' sound naturally shared even though they point to different version moments.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to finish 'final data cleanup' before Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes final data cleanup is complete once manuscript-facing tables and supplements are polished enough that co-authors will not trip over labels, wording, or visible inconsistencies.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes final data cleanup is complete only when the remaining Covidence/EndNote discrepancies, companion-record links, and note-field inconsistencies are resolved so the review archive is audit-ready.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like routine end-stage housekeeping rather than a substantive decision, and both standards are plausible forms of 'cleanup,' so the different completion thresholds remain invisible during a competent coordination discussion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Leah will 'compile the review folder' after the meeting.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the folder contains the files needed for immediate manuscript work: current draft, PRISMA figure, supplementary evidence table, and clean appendices.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the folder also includes the supporting reproducibility materials that belong with the review package, such as dated search strategies, export logs, reconciliation notes, and the master workbook.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A 'review folder' naturally sounds like a single shared container rather than a negotiated boundary, and both participants are used to broad file bundles, so neither thinks to specify where manuscript-facing contents stop and archive materials begin.

turns.inner_thought: We are four business days from co-author circulation, so this needs to stay tight. I want confirmation that the cleaned included-studies table with the 56 studies and settled theme assignments is the final extraction sheet we're all using, that the PRISMA counts already in the draft remain the latest numbers, that final data cleanup just means polishing labels and wording, and that Leah's review folder is the manuscript-facing package. If nothing changes the included set, I do not want backend file maintenance to slow the draft.
turns.utterance: Thanks for joining, Leah. Since we're so close to sending this to the co-authors, I mainly wanted to make sure we're moving from the same final extraction sheet, that the latest numbers and the current flow are settled enough for the draft, and that whatever is left under final data cleanup feeds cleanly into the review folder.

turns.inner_thought: I need this handoff to be reproducible, not just tidy. When she says final extraction sheet, I take that to mean the master workbook with all the tabs and traceability pieces. The latest numbers to me are from my most recent reconciled pass, and final data cleanup still includes getting the record trail fully consistent. When I compile the review folder, I intend to keep the manuscript files together with the supporting documentation so the package is defensible later.
turns.utterance: Yes, that makes sense. From my side, things are in good shape. Once we're comfortable with the current flow and what still counts as final data cleanup, I can compile the review folder and make sure everything travels together.

turns.inner_thought: The results section is already written around the 56 studies and the multilevel framing is settled. I need the final extraction sheet to support the tables as they stand, not reopen coding decisions or invite any remapping of themes. If the writing files are stable, we can circulate on time.
turns.utterance: That's helpful. On the writing side, the results narrative is already aligned with the 56 included studies, so I really just need the final extraction sheet to carry the manuscript tables cleanly through this last pass without us reopening the thematic structure.

turns.inner_thought: Fine by me, but the final extraction sheet still has to preserve the links, notes, and traceability that let every count and study line be followed later. I don't want to strip it down to only what appears in the manuscript and lose the reproducibility trail.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. I see this as the last pass too. I just want the final extraction sheet to hold together cleanly so anything that shows up in the supplement or appendix is still easy to follow if someone checks it later.

turns.inner_thought: The PRISMA figure in the draft already uses the counts from the last internal screening consensus meeting. I consider those the latest numbers unless something materially alters inclusion, which I don't expect. Ideally we're just smoothing presentation now.
turns.utterance: Good. And on the flow diagram, the latest numbers are already sitting in the PRISMA draft from where we left things, so my assumption is that the current flow just needs a final tidy-up before circulation rather than any real reworking.

turns.inner_thought: My current flow is the more recent reconciled version from the deduplicated export and linkage pass. I won't spell that out; I'll just proceed as though we're referring to the same current set. I'll align the appendix and records to that version.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's fine. I have the current flow updated on my end, and I'll make sure the appendix and related files line up with the latest numbers so it's all consistent when it goes out.

turns.inner_thought: As long as this doesn't expand into backend cleanup that delays us, I'm happy. Final data cleanup should stay bounded to visible polishing of the supplementary table, labels, and wording so co-authors receive a clean package Friday.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Then for me the main thing is keeping final data cleanup fairly contained over the next couple of days so the supplementary table, labels, and surrounding pieces read cleanly when the co-authors see them on Friday.

turns.inner_thought: Friday is workable, but I still mean a more complete cleanup threshold: I want the lingering discrepancies, links, and note consistency resolved enough that the archive is clean. I can say that in broad terms and she'll likely hear it as normal finishing work.
turns.utterance: Friday should still be workable. I would just like final data cleanup to cover the remaining consistency checks as well, so we're not carrying small loose ends forward once the files are in circulation.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds routine enough. After her updates, I want Leah to assemble the review folder as the stable manuscript package: draft, PRISMA figure, supplement, appendices. The real goal is getting co-author comments on the multilevel themes, not expanding process materials.
turns.utterance: That sounds reasonable. Once you've made those updates, could you compile the review folder? The immediate need on my side is a stable package for co-author comments, especially on the multilevel themes and how the results are presented.

turns.inner_thought: I'll compile the review folder as a full handoff set, including the manuscript-facing files plus the search logs, exports, version notes, and master workbook. Keeping the documentation together with the manuscript files matters if anyone later asks how we got from search to included studies.
turns.utterance: Of course. I'll compile the review folder and keep the documentation together with the main files so the package stays connected and easy to work from downstream.

turns.inner_thought: We seem aligned enough. I only want to hear about something before circulation if it changes the 56 included studies or destabilizes the narrative; otherwise I consider the rest ordinary cleanup that shouldn't interrupt the draft going out.
turns.utterance: Great. It sounds like we're aligned. Just flag anything for me before Friday only if it would materially change the 56-study story; otherwise I'd prefer we keep the momentum and send the files out as planned.

turns.inner_thought: I'll finalize the master workbook tonight, tighten the traceability pieces as much as possible, and assemble the full review folder with both the manuscript files and the reproducibility materials. From my perspective that keeps Friday on track and leaves us with a defensible record.
turns.utterance: Will do. I'll finalize the extraction sheet and compile the review folder tonight so Friday stays on track.
